parakeet: Leaving religion can free you from a doctrine, but it doesn't automatically free you from the habits that doctrine trained into you. Because if you leave religion but keep the same fear, the same certainty, the same tribalism, the same need for enemies, and the same inability to sit with complexity, then you didn't get free. You just switched teams. That's why, ever since I started sharing my story and vision publicly, I've said repeatedly that I wouldn't necessarily classify myself as anti-religious. Not because I don't believe religion causes harm. I absolutely believe religious beliefs, even when well-intentioned can provide cultural permission and social pressure to conform to norms that perpetuate harm. Religion can make people afraid to think honestly, afraid to ask better questions, afraid to leave toxic systems, and afraid to humanize people outside the group. So let me be clear. I'm not soft on the harm. I'm just not simplistic about where the harm comes from. I'm not convinced religion is the only system that bears the guilt. I don't think religion is harmful simply because religion is bad. I think religion becomes harmful because humans are often bad at complexity. The goal is not merely to stop believing religious claims. The goal is to become more honest, more thoughtful, more humane, more responsible, and more capable of living in reality without needing reality to be simple. Because the future doesn't belong to the most certain. It belongs to the people mature enough to stay curious when certainty would be much easier.
